# Decisions: typed-judge

- 2026-09-20T16:50:17.143Z — rule: **Never call a model from a hook, statusline, shim, fold or projection path, and never without the operator's opt-in; a judge call runs only inside an MCP tool, the driver, a pull command or an explicit offline command, sends redacted state, and produces advisory output only.** — chose **A narrowly scoped exception to the zero-model invariant: sofar MAY call TypeSafe Jev (a typed-decision model, no text generation) as a Judge provider, only when the operator has opted in via config, only from an MCP tool, the driver, a pull command or an explicit offline command, only with redacted state, and only to produce advisory outputs (warnings, rankings, enrichment events stamped with producer and model version). Ruled by the user 2026-09-20 ("let's come back to the Jev implementation") after the audit in roadmap-h2 note 01M2X0KK6MT2AE2A83KWJ3PZX9.** over Keeping the invariant absolute (leaves every judgement lexical and count-based; the record shows the costs in wasted stall sessions, re-proposals and adjacency-not-aboutness); a general LLM call in the engine (text generation, seconds of latency, unverifiable output — refused in roadmap-h2 note 01M2ZESQFZWVM8TYHXG19YYVZN); a local encoder model shipped with sofar (a new dependency and model weights in the hot path, and the HN finding that the hard part is the answer spaces, not the model). because Jev defeats only the cost clause of felt-cost D3 (about $0.0007 per full-digest judgement, output free) and TypeSafe contractually does not train on inputs; the privacy and dependency clauses remain, which is why the exception is opt-in, redacted, advisory and confined to paths a hook never touches (70–500 ms against the 100 ms shim budget). A default install still makes zero model calls, so SPEC Architectural invariants holds for everyone who does not opt in; this decision supersedes it and felt-cost D3 for the opted-in judge paths only.
- 2026-09-21T09:55:31.505Z — rule: **The engine never ships a direct model provider; every judge call goes through the `cloud` provider to api.sofar.sh, and the free path is the deterministic default only.** — chose **Jev is a paid feature, for now: the engine ships only the deterministic default provider and a `cloud` provider that posts redacted state and questions to a judge endpoint on api.sofar.sh, where sofar-cloud enforces the plan and calls TypeSafe with sofar's own key. Supersedes D1's direct-call clause; D1's placement, opt-in, redaction and advisory rules stand.** over A bring-your-own-key TypeSafe provider in the MIT engine (makes the feature free to anyone with a key and adds a second egress host); entitlement checks in the engine (forbidden by drive-visibility D6); shipping nothing until sofar-cloud has the endpoint (blocks the seam and the write-time guards from being built and tested against the deterministic provider). because Paid gating can only live on the server (D6), and routing through api.sofar.sh keeps the engine's single egress host (SPEC Architectural invariants, sync-client D4) while letting sofar-cloud meter usage on a plan; Jev's price (~$0.0007 per full-digest judgement) makes the margin trivial and users need no TypeSafe account. For linked repos the record is already synced, so server-side judging over synced events with enrichment events returned via pull needs nothing extra to leave the machine; only write-time guards take the round trip.
- 2026-09-21T10:32:35.107Z — chose **The cloud judge endpoint is repo-scoped: POST {api_url}/v1/repos/:repo_id/judge with body {state, questions}, amending SPEC §Judge's POST {api_url}/v1/judge (written in 2.1 before the server existed).** over Keeping the unscoped POST /v1/judge, or unscoped with repo_id in the body. because sofar-cloud's plan is per org (sofar-app SPEC, GET /v1/me/entitlement reports per-org state), and a token can belong to several orgs. An unscoped call leaves the server unable to tell which plan to charge. A repo-scoped path matches push and pull (/v1/repos/:repo_id/…), lets the server reuse the repo→org membership check it already runs, and sends only an id, never content. The server does not exist yet, so nothing is broken.

Revisit the class when 5.1 ships a writer that is not the driver (the write-back relevance pass or pull). Only summary and example change, not fields, so the schema fingerprint is untouched.
